hypothesis: The complete-cart workflow relies on acquireLockStep keyed by cart id to serialize concurrent completions. If the default locking provider only works within one process, two servers racing to complete the same cart can both pass the order_cart idempotency read before either links an order, producing two orders for one cart and two different ok order ids, which trips one_order_per_cart and possibly no_orphaned_orders. I expect at least one run to show two orders linked to the cart.

schema: oversold.scenario/v1
name: same-cart-two-servers
description: One cart is completed at the same moment through two servers sharing one database.
target:
  engine: medusa
  version: 2.22.0
  servers: 2
stock:
  SOLO: 5
carts:
  alice:
    server: 1
    lines:
    - sku: OVS-SOLO

  server: 1

  cart: alice

  server: 2
  do: complete
  cart: alice
timing:

  jitter_ms:

  - 3

hypothesis: OVS-PIECE and OVS-TWOPACK both draw on the shared WIDGET item with stock 10. If stock is checked per line and lines sharing an item are not added up, two carts that each need 6 WIDGET units (one with a TWOPACK x3, one with a PIECE x6) can both pass a per-line check against 10 and both complete, overselling WIDGET. I expect no_oversell to fail in some runs.

hypothesis: Medusa updates the inventory level reserved_quantity counter. If that counter is written from a value read earlier rather than incremented atomically, concurrent reservations on the same inventory item (from carts on different products sharing WIDGET, completed together) can lose one update, leaving reserved_quantity lower than the sum of live reservations. I expect reserved_matches_reservations to fail when several distinct carts on WIDGET complete concurrently.
